title: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education - National Value Education - Electoral Malpractices
exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
subject: National Value Education

questions.q: In Civic Education, which of the following provides the most accurate definition of **Electoral Malpractice**?
options: A peaceful transition of power from an incumbent to a newly elected official
Any illegal, fraudulent, or unconstitutional interference committed before, during, or after an election to unlawfully manipulate the outcome
The process where citizens peacefully protest an unfair government policy
The legal cancellation of an election due to severe weather conditions
questions.explain: **Electoral Malpractice** refers to any illicit, fraudulent, or corrupt act aimed at interfering with the electoral process in order to give a candidate or party an unfair advantage, ultimately subverting the will of the people.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: If a corrupt electoral official receives result sheets from a polling unit showing that Candidate A scored 100 votes, but the official intentionally changes the figure to 1,000 votes, which specific form of malpractice has occurred?
questions.explain: Altering, inflating, or deducting actual figures recorded on official result sheets to favor a specific candidate is a direct crime known as the **Manipulation of votes** (or result falsification).
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: A citizen successfully votes in the morning using a fake identity card, and later returns to the same polling unit with their real identity card to cast another ballot. This illegal act is legally termed:
questions.explain: **Multiple voting** occurs when an individual fraudulently casts more than one ballot in the same election, severely compromising the democratic principle of 'One Man, One Vote'.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Electoral officials deliberately delay the arrival of ballot boxes and voting registers in a region known to strongly support an opposition candidate. This specific strategic form of malpractice is referred to as:
questions.explain: Creating an **Artificial scarcity of electoral materials** involves deliberately delaying, hiding, or undersupplying necessary voting tools (like ballot papers and BVAS machines) to disenfranchise voters in specific opponent strongholds.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Examine the following scenario: A 15-year-old student is permitted by corrupt polling agents to cast a ballot during a general election. What specific form of electoral malpractice has just taken place?
questions.explain: The Nigerian Constitution pegs the legal voting age at 18. Allowing any person below 18 years to vote is a severe constitutional violation known as **Underage voting**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Armed youths forcefully invading a polling center, shooting sporadically into the air to scare away legitimate voters, and snatching the ballot boxes is an extreme example of:
questions.explain: **Thuggery and intimidation** involve the use of violence, weapons, or aggressive threats to disrupt the voting process, scare away opposing voters, and forcefully steal electoral materials.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: To prevent voters from making an independent choice, a politician's agent secretly distributes cash and bags of rice at the polling unit in exchange for citizens voting for their party. This highly destructive practice is known as:
questions.explain: Giving out money, food, or material gifts to sway a voter's choice illegally on election day is a major electoral crime defined as **Inducement and corrupt practices**, colloquially called 'Vote Buying'.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: During an election campaign, a candidate intentionally lies, publishing an official document promising to "construct gold-paved roads nationwide in two weeks," knowing fully well it is impossible. This fraudulent deception of the electorate falls under:
questions.explain: Publishing completely unachievable, fabricated, and blatantly deceitful campaign promises solely to trick the masses into voting is recognized as distributing **Fake manifestos**, a subtle but toxic form of malpractice.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following represents a devastating consequence of widespread electoral malpractices on a developing democracy?
options: It strictly ensures that only highly educated leaders are elected
It completely eradicates poverty in the rural areas
It leads to the emergence of illegitimate, unpopular leaders, resulting in bad governance and political violence
It highly promotes foreign direct investment and peace
questions.explain: When elections are heavily rigged, the true choice of the people is subverted. This directly leads to **illegitimate governments**, bad governance, lack of accountability, and often sparks violent political riots.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q:
Look at the list below detailing electoral activities:

1. Smuggling pre-thumbprinted ballot papers into the polling unit.
2. Arriving early to the polling unit to undergo formal BVAS accreditation.
3. Using local gangs to stop a specific tribe from voting.

Which of these activities is completely **legal** and is NOT a form of electoral malpractice?
questions.explain: Activity 2 (arriving for **formal accreditation**) is a legal and mandatory step for voting. Activities 1 (fake ballot papers) and 3 (thuggery/intimidation) are severe electoral crimes.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Inducement and corrupt practices often physically manifest at polling units in the form of **"Vote Buying"**. What is the most devastating long-term effect of vote buying on a developing democracy?
options: It permanently eradicates poverty by redistributing wealth directly to the masses
It allows highly wealthy but corrupt and incompetent candidates to bypass popular choice, leading to massive bad governance and looting
It instantly repairs the national economy by increasing the circulation of physical cash
It forces INEC to automatically upgrade to electronic voting systems
questions.explain: **Vote buying** commodifies the electoral franchise. It subverts the will of the people and allows corrupt individuals to "purchase" leadership positions. They then prioritize recouping their spent money through massive state corruption rather than providing good governance.
